explanation: Count values by their high 16 bits, choose a bucket with fewer than 65,536 entries, then rescan and mark its low 16-bit values. An unmarked low value combined with that bucket gives a missing integer. Negative signed inputs are skipped in the counting pass to avoid indexing the counter with a negative high part; they cannot equal a chosen nonnegative candidate.
timeComplexity: O(n+2^16): two stream passes, a scan of the 2^16 counters and a scan of 2^16 low-value flags. Set scanning checks at most n+1 candidates; bucket variants perform two full passes and fixed-size scans.
spaceComplexity: O(2^16) counters/flags, independent of stream length when the input can be traversed twice. Set entries, bucket arrays and Python tee buffering are explicitly accounted for above.

correctness: A bucket containing fewer entries than its 65,536 possible low values must have a hole, even with duplicate entries. The second pass marks every present low value in that bucket; an unmarked bit therefore reconstructs an absent value. This argument requires the stream to have fewer than 2^31 entries for the bank’s nonnegative signed-int output range so some bucket is underfull.
walkthrough: For [0,1,3], bucket zero has three entries and is underfull. Mark low values 0,1,3; the first unmarked position is 2. Return 2. The wrapper validates absence; true in the executable example is its verdict.
edgeCases: Duplicates may raise a bucket count but cannot falsely mark an absent low value.
An empty stream selects bucket zero and returns zero.
The underfull-bucket proof needs fewer than 2^31 stream entries for a guaranteed nonnegative signed-int answer; Python tee has an additional storage cost.
